newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS -- Issues to watch - March 17.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS -- Issues to watch - March 17.

text.p: * Dell Computer Corp was 3/8 firmer at 70-1/2 in London, helped by an article in the "Heard on the Street" column in the Wall Street Journal. But a report in investment journal Barron's that sales of personal computers were slowing hit other high-tech shares, dealers said. Compaq Computer Corp fell 3/8 to 75-1/2.
* Employee Solutions Inc gained 5/8 to 6-7/8 after-hours trade Friday, after falling 9-1/8 on Nasdaq during regular hours.

The temporary employee provider lost over 13-1/2 points the last two trading days and Friday confirmed market fears that fourth quarter earnings would not live up to Wall Street expectations. Fourth quarter earnings, released Monday, were $0.07 per share compared to a First Call estimate of $0.14.
* Tyco International Ltd said it would buy ADT Ltd in a deal worth $5.6 billion. Tyco closed at 60-1/4 and ADT closed at 21-3/4 on the NYSE.

The merger deal comes on the heels of a hostile, $3.5 billion takeover bid by Western Resources Inc for ADT, under which ADT stockholders would receive $22.50 a share. A Western Resources spokesperson was not available for comment. Western Resources closed at 30-1/8.
